text:
alex: Heads up — we started seeing a flurry of GPU OOMs on nvlink-cluster-03 ~15:30 UTC after the kernel-selection change. Multiple crashes in the runtime allocator.

alex: sample log: `RuntimeError: cuda out of memory when allocating 3221225472 bytes`

deploy-bot: deploy finished: backend/runtime/kernel-selector v3.4.1 by matt_g at 2026-03-18T15:26:40Z

matt_g: ack. immediate mitigations: open circuit-breaker for long requests, and shed KV cache aggressively.

matt_g: quick command to flip circuit breaker (prod):
```
redwoodctl routes update --route inference.prod --circuit-breaker "max_tokens=2048,concurrent_requests=120,reject=true"
```

susan: start KV shedding now: drop per-workspace kv_cache_max_bytes from 12GB -> 6GB to reclaim space while we triage.

susan: config snippet (temp):
```
runtime.kv_cache.max_bytes_per_workspace=6442450944  # 6GB
runtime.kv_cache.eviction_policy=age_based
```

priya: can we rollback kernel-selector to v3.4.0? That was stable. If we can’t do a full rollback, canary a previous kernel for 20% traffic.

kai: also set RW_WORKSPACE_MODE=conservative to force smaller workspace preallocations — it avoids the aggressive fused-attention kernel workspace growth.

alex: ran a quick profile on the failing host (nvlink-cluster-03):
```
perf_dump --node nvlink-cluster-03 --output /tmp/perf-1859.txt
# key lines:
# allocator.high_water_mark=11894783488  (11.8GB)
# kvcache.hwm=10995116288 (10.24GB)
# allocator.fragmentation_pct=28
# kernel_selector: chose fused_attention_workspace_v2 for seq_len>1024
```

matt_g: that kernel change is the suspect. fused_attention_workspace_v2 ups the temporary workspace allocation for certain seq lengths. If kernel_selector misclassifies sequence distribution, we hit huge preallocs.

priya: plan: 1) short-term: flip circuit breaker + kv shedding + conservative workspace 2) mid-term: rollback kernel-selector or canary 3) add a request-shaping policy to truncate sequences > 2048 before hitting runtime.

susan: request-shaping example rule (gateway):
```
# gateway truncation rule
if request.tokens > 2048:
  request.tokens = 2048
  add_header X-Redwood-Shape: truncated
```

kai: fallback option: route to quantized model variant (gpt-large-q4) for 30% of traffic. quantized model has much smaller workspace and KV pressure.

matt_g: put together a canary rollout:
- set kernel-selector to v3.4.0 for 20% of inference.prod
- route 30% to gpt-large-q4 fallback model
- keep circuit-breaker enabled global

alex: executing steps now: 1) applied KV max_bytes_per_workspace -> 6GB on cluster 03/04/05 2) set RW_WORKSPACE_MODE=conservative on those nodes 3) pushed a circuit-breaker update (max_tokens=2048)

deploy-bot: route update applied: inference.prod circuit-breaker updated by alex at 2026-03-18T15:34:12Z

alex: monitoring — allocator HWM dropped from 11.8GB -> 8.7GB after shedding; no new OOMs in last 6 mins. CPU latency stable.

priya: next steps for a proper postmortem: collect kernel-selection trace, sequence length histogram for last 24h, and allocator free-list metrics. I'll open a perf regression ticket and tag eng-runtime + eng-ml.

matt_g: agree. add a unit/regression test in the kernel selector harness that simulates heavy long-seq traffic and checks workspace delta.

susan: I'll keep the temporary kv limits for 24h and then gradually relax after we validate the kernel selector.

kai: also add an autoshrink policy to KV cache: if allocator fragmentation > 25% && hwm>8GB -> force extra eviction cycle. That buys us safety for the future.

alex: thanks all. recording these steps in the incident playbook and will follow up with timeline + rolled changes. :thumbsup:
